title: Redwood Security Review - SSO/SCIM/RBAC (FinTechCo)
summary: Redwood AE + SE walked FinTechCo through SSO (SAML) and SCIM provisioning options and reviewed RBAC best practices for least-privilege access. Key concerns were IdP attribute mappings, group sync cadence, delegated admin roles, audit log retention, and KMS key management. Action items: exchange SAML metadata, share RBAC mapping doc, FinTechCo to provide IdP metadata and test account, Redwood to share SOC 2 report and KMS whitepaper.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-18
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Head of Security - FinTechCo), Miguel Alvarez (IT Ops), Samir Kapoor (Platform Engineer)

Summary: SSO (SAML) + SCIM provisioning walkthrough, RBAC least-privilege model review, audit logs and KMS discussion.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Jordan here, I'm the AE on the account, with Maya our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Priya Nair: good, thanks. We're excited to dig into SSO and RBAC, we've got some compliance questions.
[00:10] Miguel Alvarez: hey, thanks. We just want to make sure integration fits our IdP and we can keep audit trails for audits.
[00:18] Maya Patel: great, we'll run through SAML metadata, SCIM provisioning, and then show how our RBAC maps to least-privilege. We'll also cover audit logs retention and keys.
[00:25] Jordan Lee: quick agenda: SAML setup details, SCIM provisioning for group sync, RBAC patterns, audit logging + KMS notes, then next steps. Does that work?
[00:32] Priya Nair: yes. Also, short question: we are bound by SOC 2 and need encryption at rest w/ customer-managed keys.
[00:38] Jordan Lee: absolutely, we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and have envelope encryption for hosted; we'll share the KMS whitepaper.
[00:44] Maya Patel: jumping into SAML — our SP supports SAML2.0. We can accept IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows. The key fields we need are: EntityID, Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) URL, NameID format, and attribute mappings for username/email and groups.
[00:58] Miguel Alvarez: good, we use Okta. For groups we prefer mapping via group membership assertions, not SCIM only.
[01:05] Maya Patel: that's fine; we support groups via SAML assertions and SCIM. Note that SAML group assertions are not always consistent, SCIM gives canonical group state.
[01:12] Priya Nair: how do you handle group changes and admin roles? We need least-privilege, and only a tiny team should be able to create service-level keys.
[01:20] Maya Patel: we recommend a few roles: org-admin (very limited for Redwood console admin), security-admin (view/edit security settings incl. SSO), infra-operator (deploy/configure inference capacity), and app-service (limited to API keys). We can map these to Okta groups via SCIM group sync and SAML group assertion.
[01:35] Jordan Lee: to add, we support delegated admin scoping so you can limit admin privileges by project or environment. Most customers do a two-admin model: security and infra.
[01:44] Samir Kapoor: sounds good. For SCIM, do you support incremental syncs, and what's the provisioning cadence?
[01:51] Maya Patel: we support delta/ incremental SCIM syncs; default is every 10 minutes for Dedicated and Private; for hosted customers it's 15 minutes. You can also trigger on-demand syncs.
[02:02] Miguel Alvarez: ok that cadence works. One requirement: audit logs need to show changes to role assignments with timestamp and the actor. How long are logs retained?
[02:11] Jordan Lee: by default, audit logs are retained 90 days on hosted, but we offer extended retention packs. For Dedicated/Private you can push logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3 with configurable retention. We'll share the doc.
[02:22] Priya Nair: and is the audit trail tamper-evident? We need chain-of-custody for some requests.
[02:27] Maya Patel: we provide signed event metadata and integrity checks; for high-security customers we recommend pushing to customer-owned S3 or SIEM that enforces WORM.
[02:36] Jordan Lee: also, our SCIM provisioning preserves source of truth flags so you can see if a change came from IdP or Redwood console — that helps for audits.
[02:44] Miguel Alvarez: good. About KMS: we want to manage CMK in our AWS account. Is that supported?
[02:50] Maya Patel: yes for Private deployments and our VPC option you can supply a customer-managed key in your AWS account; for hosted we offer envelope encryption where we manage keys but can integrate with external KMS via AWS KMS grants for dedicated customers — we'll include specifics in the KMS whitepaper.
[03:05] Samir Kapoor: are there API controls for key rotation? We need to rotate monthly and have rotation logs.
[03:11] Maya Patel: key rotation is customer-managed; rotation events are logged. If you use CMK in your account, rotation is handled by AWS KMS and we surface the events in the audit logs.
[03:20] Priya Nair: can you walk through the SAML attribute mapping? We need NameID to be persistent and use email as fallback.
[03:27] Maya Patel: we recommend persistent NameID with eduPersonScopedAffiliation when available, but most customers map NameID to email or a unique user ID (sub). For groups, we accept an attribute like 'groups' with either full DN or plain group names — we'll normalize.
[03:42] Jordan Lee: I want to call out SCIM vs SAML for provisioning: SCIM is authoritative for membership state, SAML is fine for assertions. If you rely on SAML only you risk race conditions when a user is deactivated in IdP — SCIM ensures immediate deprovisioning.
[03:54] Miguel Alvarez: we definitely want SCIM deprovisioning. Any gotchas?
[03:58] Maya Patel: watch group naming collisions and nested groups; we recommend flattening group structure and using a canonical prefix. Also ensure your IdP supports 'bulk' SCIM operations if you have many users.
[04:12] Priya Nair: what about SCIM scopes — can we limit which groups get provisioned to Redwood?
[04:17] Maya Patel: yes, we support scoping by group filter on the IdP side and mapping rules on our end. We can also do attribute-based mapping so only groups with a specific attribute sync.
[04:26] Jordan Lee: moving to RBAC best practices — most FinTech customers build a least-privilege model with role tiers per environment: prod-readonly, prod-deploy, prod-admin, staging-admin, etc. We can seed roles for you.
[04:39] Samir Kapoor: do API keys inherit RBAC? We want machine accounts with narrow scopes.
[04:43] Maya Patel: yes API keys are scoped to roles and projects; you can create service principals with token lifetimes and optional IP allowlist.
[04:50] Miguel Alvarez: can we restrict which keys can be used from which network ranges?
[04:53] Jordan Lee: yes IP allowlisting is supported and we also support VPC egress rules for Private deployments.
[04:59] Priya Nair: SAML assertions sometimes drop group info for larger tokens. Do you have a size limit?
[05:04] Maya Patel: large assertions can be an issue; SCIM is recommended for bulk membership. For SAML we also support referencing groups via group IDs rather than full lists, and then fetch on demand.
[05:16] Miguel Alvarez: about onboarding: what's the typical timeline to go from SSO config to full SCIM provisioning and RBAC mapping?
[05:21] Jordan Lee: usually 1-2 weeks: SAML config & test within 2-3 days, SCIM provisioning and role mapping another week depending on internal approvals and number of groups.
[05:31] Priya Nair: any edge cases around multiple IdPs? We have some federated teams that use a secondary IdP.
[05:36] Maya Patel: we support multiple IdPs per organization; you can set IdP priority and mapping rules. For cross-IdP group consolidation we'd recommend a single source of truth via SCIM from an authoritative IdP.
[05:48] Jordan Lee: quick note on sessions: session length defaults to 12 hours for console and tokens expire per token type; we can shorten session durations for higher security.
[05:58] Samir Kapoor: do you record session events in audit logs? We need to know token issue/refresh events.
[06:03] Maya Patel: yes, token issuance, refresh, and revocation are logged with actor and IP.
[06:08] Miguel Alvarez: what encryption algorithms do you use for data at rest?
[06:12] Maya Patel: AES-256 for data at rest, TLS1.2+ for transit; for envelope we use AES-GCM with KMS wrapping. We'll include algorithm details in the whitepaper.
[06:22] Priya Nair: good. Another compliance question: do you provide signed attestation for audit requests?
[06:27] Jordan Lee: we have SOC 2 Type II reports and can provide a custom security questionnaire under NDA. For attestation we can provide exported logs and signed artifacts depending on the engagement.
[06:36] Miguel Alvarez: ok, regarding delegated admin scoping — can an admin be scoped to only a single project so they can't affect prod?
[06:41] Maya Patel: yes, we have project-scoped roles. You can define role bindings per project and limit what a given admin can do.
[06:47] Priya Nair: how do you prevent a siloed admin from elevating privileges? Is there an approval workflow?
[06:52] Maya Patel: we provide role change audit trails and support optional manual approval workflows via API hooks to your ticketing system; we can also require MFA for console-level changes.
[07:02] Jordan Lee: single-sign-on enforcement plus conditional access on your IdP helps prevent rogue elevation.
[07:07] Samir Kapoor: any notes on provisioning service accounts for CI/CD? We don't want long-lived keys in code.
[07:13] Maya Patel: best practice is short-lived tokens with a rotation cadence and using our ephemeral token service integrated with KMS; we can scope tokens to a single pipeline with IP restrictions.
[07:23] Miguel Alvarez: is there an automated way to revoke all keys if we detect compromise?
[07:27] Maya Patel: yes we have bulk revoke APIs and org-level key rotation; revocations are immediate and logged.
[07:33] Priya Nair: great, on data residency — we need all prod data to remain in EU regions. Does Redwood support region pinning?
[07:40] Jordan Lee: yes, you can pin deployments to specific regions and we provide region-restricted storage options for EU customers; for Private we support on-prem if needed.
[07:49] Maya Patel: note that for hosted EU we ensure customer data at rest stays within the region and we provide audit logs reflecting the residency.
[07:57] Miguel Alvarez: what's the process for key escrow if we need to hand over keys for a legal request?
[08:02] Jordan Lee: for customer-managed KMS, keys are in your account so you control escrow. For hosted with Redwood-managed keys, we have a formal legal process and can provide logs and signed export under court order; we'll route that through legal.
[08:16] Priya Nair: on SCIM — the attribute mappings for role assignment are important. Can you accept custom attributes for entitlement?
[08:22] Maya Patel: yes SCIM supports custom attributes; we can map entitlements to RBAC roles via a mapping table. We'll provide a template mapping file.
[08:31] Samir Kapoor: any rate limits on SCIM calls if we have heavy churn?
[08:35] Maya Patel: we have per-tenant throttling; for high churn customers we offer burst allowances and a dedicated pipeline with higher limits.
[08:45] Miguel Alvarez: ok. Are service logs signed and tamper-proof if we push them to our S3?
[08:50] Maya Patel: if you push logs to your S3 with write-once policies or to a SIEM with immutability enabled, that achieves tamper-evidence; we also sign events before shipping.
[08:59] Jordan Lee: i'd like to demo the RBAC mapping page quickly — Maya, can you share your screen?
[09:05] Maya Patel: sure, I'm going to describe if screen isn't working: we have a mapping UI where you define role name, allowed actions, resource scope, and then attach Okta group or SCIM group id. You can preview permissions.
[09:21] Priya Nair: looks good. Can we export the mapping for audit?
[09:25] Maya Patel: yes export as CSV or JSON with timestamps.
[09:29] Samir Kapoor: small nit: when SCIM deprovisions we want to ensure service principals are not accidentally terminated. Can you exempt service accounts?
[09:36] Maya Patel: yes we support a SCIM filter to exclude users with a specific attribute like serviceAccount=true so they won't be deprovisioned automatically.
[09:46] Miguel Alvarez: thanks. For testing, what's your recommended test plan?
[09:50] Jordan Lee: recommended plan: 1) exchange metadata and configure IdP in staging, 2) run Okta/IdP-initiated login test, 3) enable SCIM in staging and run group sync, 4) map roles and run permission tests, 5) verify audit logs and KMS integration. We can help on the call.
[10:06] Priya Nair: timeline and owners?
[10:09] Jordan Lee: we'll send the integration guide today, Maya will send RBAC mapping template, Miguel to provide IdP metadata, Samir to create test user. Then schedule a follow-up to run end-to-end.
[10:20] Priya Nair: that works. A few clarifying Qs: 1) do you support SAML force-authn? 2) can we restrict sessions to internal IPs? 3) do you offer SSO session inactivity timeouts?
[10:31] Maya Patel: 1) yes forceAuthn is supported, 2) IP restriction is supported for API keys and we can do IdP conditional access for console sessions, 3) inactivity timeouts are configurable per org.
[10:42] Miguel Alvarez: internal question — if we have to change key rotation schedule, is there maintenance downtime?
[10:47] Maya Patel: no downtime when rotating CMKs; envelopes are rewrapped and read continues. We'll provide the rotation procedure.
[10:55] Jordan Lee: i'm going to capture action items now.
[10:58] Jordan Lee: Jordan to send SAML/SP metadata + integration guide (due 12/20). Maya to send RBAC mapping template (due 12/21). FinTechCo to provide IdP metadata and test account (Miguel - due 12/22). Jordan to share SOC 2 and KMS whitepaper (due 12/19). Samir to create SCIM test user and validate schema (due 12/23).
[11:25] Priya Nair: thanks, one last thing — are there standard SLAs for security incident response?
[11:31] Jordan Lee: yes enterprise customers have incident SLA tiers; we can share the SLA doc. For high-impact incidents we have on-call 24/7.
[11:38] Maya Patel: we'll include contact escalation paths in the doc.
[11:42] Miguel Alvarez: cool. Anything else?
[11:44] Priya Nair: no, that covers it. We'll expect the docs and test plan.
[11:47] Jordan Lee: great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the attachments and a link to schedule the config call.
[11:53] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional noise and overlapping talk, some proper nouns may be mis-transcribed (e.g., IdP vendor specifics), timestamps approximate.
